subject: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO calibration, streaming concurrency, and traffic profile asks
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Park <lina@mayasystems.com>, Samir Khatri <samir@latticemetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO calibration, streaming concurrency, and traffic profile asks

Hi Lina / Samir —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can scope a targeted hosted evaluation: 

1) Target SLOs
- You noted current production objectives: p95 end-to-end = 220ms, p99 = 680ms (measured at edge to UI render).
- LatticeMetrics would like Redwood hosted to demonstrate parity under the same traffic mix before procurement discussion.

2) Traffic profile (you said you would provide sample CSV)
- Mix: 75% short inference (user prompts avg 20 tokens -> model output ~40 tokens), 20% medium (avg 120 tokens in/out), 5% long-form (chained streaming, avg 600 input, streaming out).
- Concurrency baseline: 120 concurrent active users (steady), with spikes to 420 concurrent during bursts.
- Peak sustained TPS: 16 requests/s, burst TPS: 60 req/s for 90s windows.

3) Streaming and concurrency specifics
- Streaming: low-latency token-by-token streaming for the long-form path; you need first-token latency < 250ms and sustained per-token latency that keeps UI feeling live.
- KV cache: you expect heavy prefix reuse for personalized prompts (~40% cache hits).

4) Acceptance criteria for hosted POC
- Redwood to run a 48-hour hosted trial against a dataset you will share, capturing p95/p99 end-to-end under production-like routing (including CDN + regional hops).
- Success: p95 within +20% of your current baseline and p99 within +40% while preserving semantic quality.

Next steps (agreed):
- Lina: share the sample traffic CSV and a short list of 10 representative prompts + expected token counts (by EOD Wed).
- Samir: provide the DNS test endpoint + a sanitized telemetry snippet showing how you measure client-to-render latency (to align metrics).
- Ben/Laura/Jasmine: we’ll assemble a scoped proposal and a hosted-run plan (targeting a 48-hour window) and send the SLO test script and Grafana access.

I attached the call recording and a first-pass SLO proposal (PDF) and a template CSV for traffic. If that all looks good I’ll schedule the Redwood-hosted POC kickoff for next week.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com]
Redwood Inference

Attachments: lm_call_recording-20270920.mp3 (audio), redwood-slo-proposal-20270920.pdf (proposal), p95p99-traffic-snapshot.csv (sample template)

From: Samir Khatri <samir@latticemetrics.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO calibration, streaming concurrency, and traffic profile asks

Thanks Jasmine — good notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The p95/p99 numbers I quoted are measured at the client SDK level (browser -> render), which includes 15–25ms CDN overhead and ~45ms average regional hop. We’ll attach the sanitized telemetry CSV (coming shortly).
- For streaming, the UI expects first-token delivery within 220–300ms for the long-form scenario; after first token, average per-token latency should be <15ms to maintain progressive rendering.
- Regarding KV cache: the 40% figure is a best estimate; we’ll include prefix overlap stats in the CSV.

One ask from engineering: during the hosted POC we’ll exercise fallback model routing (incumbent -> fallback) — can Redwood demonstrate the failover path and provide traces for cross-checking? We prefer a brief canary with model fallback for the mid-PoC spike window.

I’ll upload the sample CSV and a sanitized telemetry snippet to the Drive link you provided.

—Samir
Samir Khatri
Head of Platform, LatticeMetrics
samir@latticemetrics.com

Nice summary Jas. Quick notes from our side before we square the hosted-run plan: 

- Model selection: propose we run the POC on Redwood-curated Llama-3-Chat-q4f16 (8-bit quant) + smaller fallback policy using a trimmed 4k context variant. That gets us representative per-token latency and realistic quality.
- Traffic shaping: we should replay the CSV at three load windows: baseline (16 TPS), ramp (peak 60 TPS for 90s), and sustained spike (30 TPS for 20 min) to validate caching behavior.
- Streaming concurrency: simulate 120 steady concurrent streams and a burst to 420 concurrent. For streaming shelf-life, instrument per-token latencies and first-byte timing and expose them on a temporary Grafana dashboard.
- Acceptance: define automated pass/fail checks in the runbook (p95/p99 thresholds, token-loss/noise checks, and semantic quality spot-checks).

I’ll draft the runbook and the JMeter/Locust config this afternoon and attach to HubSpot deal LM-8345. Jasmine — can you inline the exact metrics names LatticeMeasures will provide so we align (client_to_render, server_processing, first_token_ts)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Thanks all — attaching the sanitized artifacts as promised. 

Quick confirmations:
- We will run the POC against the Redwood-hosted endpoint. We will provide a short list of 10 golden prompts and a 48-hour traffic CSV (you will treat the CSV as exact request timing for replay).
- Our acceptance panel will check p95/p99 client_to_render and do three semantic spot checks after the run.
- We accept a one-time +40% leeway on p99 for the hosted trial if the semantic regressions are within an agreed threshold.

A couple of asks for Redwood engineering:
- Please confirm what Telemetry fields you will expose in Grafana (server_processing_ms, first_token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_fallback_count).
- Confirm whether Redwood hosted will run the fallback policy we discussed and surface traces for any fallback events.

If you confirm those two items I’ll lock the kickoff window late next week.

Best,
Lina Park
Director of Product, Maya Systems (LatticeMetrics partner)
lina@mayasystems.com
